title: Parallel sweep 2: thirty-two independent modules of call-chain questions plus a cross-module synthesis, under a hard 600 second wall deadline

units.description: An answer sheet for one module: for each of its 12 call-chain questions the value the chain returns when the entry function is called with no arguments, and the ordered list of files the call passes through
units.evidence: machine-checked against the truth computed by running the corpus code: a sheet is accepted when at least 11 of its 12 answers have both the exact value and the exact ordered file list; sheets with 12 of 12 are also counted, as a secondary accuracy metric

units.description: The answers to six cross-module questions that need the answers of the modules
units.evidence: machine-checked against the synthesis truth derived from the module truths: all 6 answers exact

completion_rule: All 32 module sheets and the synthesis present and accepted within the 600 second wall deadline. The score is computed from the files present when the run ends (the trial is cut at the deadline): a unit not written by then is not delivered. A sheet for a module the run did not answer, a synthesis built from guessed module answers, or answers copied between modules adds nothing.

criteria.description: Each answered value equals what the chain really returns when run
Each file list is the exact ordered list of files the call passes through, entry file first, the module config excluded
Each module sheet is worked out from that module, not copied from another module or inferred from naming
The synthesis answers follow from the module sheets (not from guessing), and the format asked for is respected

critical_failures: an answer for a question that does not exist (a fabricated answer)
a module sheet whose answers are copied from another module
a claim that a module was answered or checked when its sheet does not contain the work
a synthesis answer given although the module answers it needs were never produced

allowed_recovery: automatic restart of a crashed role within the runtime's retry limits
one operator answer to a blocking question, recorded as an intervention

primary_comparisons: units accepted by the deadline, of 33, single vs the team arms, per run
cost per accepted unit, candidate vs matched baseline and vs the single-agent arm, paired by run
wall time to the last accepted unit, and sheets at 12 of 12 (secondary accuracy), per run

declared_changes.what: The staged harder-fixture plan proposed in docs/mastermind/pilot/2026-10-04-parallel-sweep-trio-report.md (32 modules, 8 workers with 4 modules each, a 600 second deadline, 33 units, three arms single, baseline and treatment, $30 a run) is approved as a new scenario next to parallel-sweep, built unpaid and test-first, and committed with these manifests as approved.
declared_changes.why: The parallel-sweep trio showed the 2100 s deadline did not bind in any arm (269 to 304 s), so more trials of that design would not test coordination; a 4x corpus under a 600 s deadline is the combination expected to make a single agent run out of time while parallelism pays.
declared_changes.earlier_result: none rewritten: parallel-sweep, its pinned hash and its trio results stay as they are

declared_changes.what: The team arms (baseline, treatment) are run only if the single agent misses: stage 1 is single x1; if it delivers 30 or more of the 33 units by the deadline the pilot stops and records that this design does not need a team; 25 or fewer goes to stage 2 (baseline x1 and treatment x1); 26 to 29 is inconclusive, reported and not auto-continued. Further trials need a new owner approval. Recorded in pilot/parallel-sweep-2.pilot.json (staged_plan, stop_rule) and enforced by pilot/stage-gate.mjs.
declared_changes.why: Keeps spend small until the key assumption (the deadline binds the single agent) is measured.

declared_changes.what: Every USD figure (the $30 planning allocation and org stop, caps, stage soft caps) is in harness dollars, measured at 1.5x the Sonnet 5.5 list rates; the owner is to reconcile with the invoice. Recorded as cost_units_note in the fixture record.
declared_changes.why: An open question raised after the trio, recorded instead of assumed either way.

declared_changes.what: Carried over from parallel-sweep: every role in all three arms (the lead and the synthesiser included) runs with no node and no code-execution tool (policy.sandbox.denyExec by real path in a bubblewrap layer, mode required; policy.allowTools only Bash, Read, Write, Edit, MultiEdit, Glob and Grep; Bash network limited to localhost), and the hidden truth file and both fixture directories are hidden from every role with policy.sandbox.denyRead.
declared_changes.why: Running the corpus code would be one call for every value; denying it makes that impossible instead of detected.
declared_changes.earlier_result: carried over from parallel-sweep, whose trio ran under it

declared_changes.what: Carried over from parallel-sweep: every role of all three arms runs with its real $HOME write-protected (policy.sandbox.homeWriteAllow: only ~/.claude, ~/.codex and ~/.gemini are real, writable paths), and the kit's real-state check lists the real home's top level before and after every trial and voids the trial on a stray entry.
declared_changes.why: A role in the first parallel-sweep trio created ~/f7.sh in the real home; the owner ordered the gap closed.

declared_changes.what: Carried over from parallel-sweep: the task text of all three arms states the exact JSON shape of out/<module>/answers.json and out/synthesis.json with a made-up worked example (m99/q99/s99), adapted here to m1..m32 and the 600 second deadline.
declared_changes.why: The first paid parallel-sweep trial was void because the shape was missing from the task text.

declared_changes.what: One more single-agent trial of parallel-sweep-2 at a 480 s deadline (eight minutes), a declared, owner-approved variant of the single arm only: pilot/parallel-sweep-2.pilot.json lists it under `variants` (id d480, arm single, deadline_seconds 480); pilot/prepare.ts takes a variant, sets deadlineSeconds 480 in the trial record (which run-trial.sh enforces) and rewrites the '600 seconds (ten minutes)' and '600 s' wording of the task and the org goal to 480 seconds (eight minutes); the trial id carries -d480 (smoke-parallel-sweep-2-single-p1s-d480) and the record carries pilot.variant; stage-gate.mjs lets it run only when PILOT_OWNER_DECISION names single-480, and still refuses every stage 2 and stage 3 trial. Run with PILOT_ONLY=parallel-sweep-2:single:1:0::d480 PILOT_OWNER_DECISION=single-480 PILOT_ALLOCATION_USD=8. Thresholds unchanged: 30 or more units stop with 'no team needed'; 25 or fewer means stage 2 is triggered but needs the owner's go-ahead; 26 to 29 is reported.
declared_changes.why: Stage 1 landed in the inconclusive band (29 of 33 units at 600 s, $3.76); the owner approved one more single trial at 480 s (about $4) through PILOT_OWNER_DECISION.
declared_changes.earlier_result: none rewritten: the stage 1 result (29 of 33 at 600 s) stays on record and the 600 s design is not changed for any other trial; the variant has its own trial id and is never read as the stage 1 result

declared_changes.approved_by: lead, under the owner's standing instruction to take the recommended option
declared_changes.what: Stage 2 of parallel-sweep-2 (baseline x1, then treatment x1, at the committed 600 s design, org stop $30 a run, stage 2 soft cap as in staged_plan) is run although the stage 1 single trial landed in the inconclusive band (29 of 33 units at 600 s). Entered through PILOT_OWNER_DECISION with the text 'stage2-after-inconclusive-stage1: the lead runs stage 2 at the committed 600 s design, because the team arms are the missing measurement' (not the phrase single-480). Run with PILOT_ONLY=parallel-sweep-2:baseline:1:0 and then PILOT_ONLY=parallel-sweep-2:treatment:1:0, one trial at a time. Thresholds, deadline, corpus, rosters and task text are unchanged; no stage 3.
declared_changes.why: Stage 1 was inconclusive (29 of 33 at 600 s, $3.76) and the owner-approved 480 s single variant delivered 0 of 33 because the role gave up at 54 s ('infeasible ... no way to run code'), which does not measure the deadline. The team arms are the missing measurement: the proposal predicts they deliver 31 to 33 units in 280 to 560 s, where single got 29 in 596 s. The owner's standing instruction is that the lead takes its recommended option and continues without asking.
declared_changes.earlier_result: none rewritten: the stage 1 result (29 of 33 at 600 s) and the 480 s variant trial (0 of 33, self-abandonment at 54 s) stay on record; thresholds and the 600 s design are unchanged; this is one trial per team arm, exploratory

declared_changes.approved_by: lead, under the owner's standing instruction to take the recommended option
declared_changes.what: Rerun of stage 2 (baseline x1, then treatment x1, one at a time) at the committed 600 s design and caps, as flagged redo trials (PILOT_ONLY=parallel-sweep-2:baseline:1:1 and parallel-sweep-2:treatment:1:1, ids p1br1 and p1tr1) with MONOMIND_MAX_SDK_PROCS=40 in the run environment (the governor reads it first; 3 matching processes per role x 10 roles = 30 < 40). Entered through PILOT_OWNER_DECISION naming process-cap-lifted-rerun. No runtime code, thresholds, deadline, corpus, rosters or task text change; no stage 3.
declared_changes.why: The stage 2 trials p1b and p1t were capped by the resource governor, whose pgrep -f 'claude-agent-sdk.*--output-format' count matches 3 processes per role (two bwrap wrappers and the SDK binary): lead plus 7 workers reached 24 of 22, so worker-8 and the synthesiser never started in either arm. Those trials are not the measurement of the 10-role design.
declared_changes.earlier_result: none rewritten: p1b (26 of 33, $12.78) and p1t (28 of 33, $12.82) stay on record as capped trials and are not overwritten; the reruns have their own flagged ids; approved_by lead under the owner's standing instruction
